title: Sampling Design: Random, Stratified & Cluster Sampling
interviewAnswer: Sampling design determines which population the data represents. Simple random sampling gives each unit equal probability; stratification samples within known groups; cluster sampling selects groups and can increase correlation/variance.
keyPoints: Sampling mechanism affects both bias and standard error.
Stratification can improve precision for important subgroups.
why: Sampling Design: Random, Stratified & Cluster Sampling is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
intuition: Sampling mechanism affects both bias and standard error.
deepDive: Sampling design determines which population the data represents. Simple random sampling gives each unit equal probability; stratification samples within known groups; cluster sampling selects groups and can increase correlation/variance. Stratification can improve precision for important subgroups. Clustered samples need clustered uncertainty. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: Estimate customer satisfaction by stratifying across regions rather than letting the largest region dominate a convenience sample.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.

production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
